explanation.text: The Logic: The Treynor ratio measures excess return per unit of systematic risk: (Rp − Rf) / beta_p. Standard deviation in the Sharpe ratio is replaced by beta in the Treynor ratio, isolating market-related risk because unsystematic risk can be diversified away in a well-diversified portfolio. The Trap: (Rp − Rf)/sigma_p is the Sharpe ratio, not Treynor. Rp/beta_p omits the risk-free rate and therefore does not measure excess return. sigma_p/beta_p is a risk-only ratio with no return component. Note: Distributor-style pro-tip and cross-exam framing removed; explanation grounded in pp.148 and 150 (Treynor formula, beta replaces sigma, diversifiable unsystematic risk).
